I’ve started buying AVGO in small increments; I believe the long-term outlook for the AI trade remains intact, and Broadcom has been unfairly punished, given that its business incorporates one of the world’s strongest lock-in effects—with custom-designed AI chips and infrastructure, along with customers who would be extremely costly and time-consuming to switch away from. Revenue from AI semiconductors has increased by 221% year-over-year, and the stock has slipped about 30% since its peak in June. There are risks, of course—for example, 50% of quarterly revenue comes from a single distributor—but I don’t see any chance whatsoever that this customer would terminate the relationship or switch partners for its solutions. I see a good risk/reward ratio over the next several years and am slowly building up my position in my “Buy, Hold, and Monitor” portfolio.
